events.title: US Consumer Prices Rise More Than Expected In October
events.summary: US consumer prices rose a seasonally adjusted 0.4 percent in October, more than expected, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on 10 November. Core prices, which exclude food and energy, rose 0.3 percent, also more than expected. The bureau did not estimate a yearly inflation rate because last year's government shutdown prevented it from collecting data.

events.title: US Charges Three Alleged Iran-Backed Operatives Over Attacks In Europe And US
events.summary: Federal prosecutors in New York unsealed an eight-count superseding indictment on 10 November charging three men with terrorism-related offences over nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks in Europe and the United States, which the Justice Department says were carried out in support of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Iraqi militia Kata'ib Hizballah. The charges include a September 2026 plot at RAF Fairford in England, where US forces were stationed, and an attempt to bomb a synagogue in New York. One of the men, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, has been in US custody since May; the others are Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani.

events.title: Idaho Man Sentenced To 18 Years Over ISIS-Inspired Church Attack Plot
events.summary: Alexander Scott Mercurio, 21, of Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, was sentenced in federal court on 10 November to 18 years in prison for attempting to provide material support to the Islamic State group, the Justice Department said. Prosecutors said he had planned to take his father's firearms for a mass-casualty attack on Idaho churches "in the name of ISIS", and also planned to use explosives, knives and a machete. The FBI arrested him on 6 April 2024, one day before the planned attack.

events.title: House Shelves Effort To Impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth
events.summary: The House of Representatives voted 211 to 204 on 10 November to refer articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, effectively ending the effort. Republican Representative Thomas Massie, who filed the resolution with eight articles of impeachment largely over the war with Iran, was the only Republican to vote with Democrats against the referral.

events.title: US Measles Cases Reach Highest Level Since 1991
events.summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 5,182 confirmed measles cases in the United States so far in 2026, the highest annual total since 1991 and more than double the 2,289 cases recorded in 2025. Four people have died of measles this year.

events.title: Catastrophic Flood Hits Tennessee-Georgia State Line
events.summary: Storms caused catastrophic flooding along the Tennessee–Georgia state line on 5 November, described as a 1-in-1,000-year flood event. Swift-water teams rescued dozens of people in the twin towns of McCaysville, Georgia, and Copperhill, Tennessee, and a 56-year-old woman died in floodwaters in Murray County, Georgia. Governor Brian Kemp declared a state of emergency for four counties.

events.title: Twelve Illinois Counties Back Non-Binding Separation Referendums
events.summary: Voters in 12 more Illinois counties approved non-binding referendums on 3 November supporting separation from the state, citing the political influence of Chicago and Cook County, FOX 32 Chicago reported. Voters in 45 counties have now approved such measures since 2020. The votes are advisory; creating a new state would require approval from the Illinois General Assembly and Congress.

events.title: Democrats Win Control Of Both Houses Of Congress
events.summary: Democrats won majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the 3 November midterm elections, Ballotpedia reported. Al Jazeera reported that the party had won control of the Senate. Some individual races were still uncalled while ballots were counted.

events.title: Nine Killed As Business Jet Crashes In Florida
events.summary: A Learjet 60 flying from Austin, Texas, to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas crashed near South Military Trail in Palm Beach County, Florida, near Greenacres, on 1 November, killing all nine people on board. The NTSB said the crew had reported light clear ice and moderate turbulence shortly before the crash.

events.title: Eleven Shot Near Florida A&M Stadium After Homecoming Game
events.summary: Eleven people, including six juveniles, were shot near Bragg Memorial Stadium at Florida A&M University in Tallahassee on the night of 24 October, hours after the school's homecoming football game. Twelve people were injured in all, and police said the shooting followed a physical altercation among people who knew one another. A 15-year-old will be charged as an adult.

motive.attributedTo: Tallahassee police, who said it stemmed from an altercation among a small group

events.title: Chemical Tank Rupture Forces Evacuations In Toledo
events.summary: A tank ruptured at MC Tank Transport in north Toledo, Ohio, on the night of 20 October, releasing glycidyl methacrylate, an industrial chemical used in plastics, paints and coatings. People within one mile were evacuated and those within three miles were told to shelter in place. By 23 October the city had lifted the evacuation orders after crews found no detectable hazards.

events.title: National Guard Member Shot While Breaking Up Fight In Washington
events.summary: A National Guard member deployed in Washington, D.C., was shot in the leg on the night of 18 October while breaking up a fight in the Eastern Market neighbourhood, police said. Police said the suspect pointed a gun at the troops and was shot in return fire, then arrested. Both injuries were described as non-life-threatening.

events.title: No Kings Protests Held Nationwide Ahead Of Midterms
events.summary: Hundreds of No Kings rallies against President Donald Trump's administration drew crowds in New York and other US cities on 17 October. This round aimed to get people out to vote early ahead of the 3 November midterm elections.

events.title: Three Children And A Teacher Killed In Oregon School Shooting
events.summary: A 16-year-old opened fire at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on 15 October, killing three children and a teacher, according to police. The suspected shooter was then shot and killed by a bystander.
